earnings.title: Media Inquiries:
highlights: Deere Reports Net Income of $1.051 Billion for Fourth Quarter, $4.860 Billion for Fiscal Year

MOLINE, Illinois (November 25, 2026) — Deere & Company reported net income of $1.051 billion for the fourth quarter ended November 1, 2026, or $3.89 per share, compared with net income of $1.065 billion, or $3.93 per share, for the quarter ended November 2, 2025.
For fiscal year 2026, net income attributable to Deere & Company was $4.860 billion, or $17.95 per share, compared with $5.027 billion, or $18.50 per share, in fiscal 2025.
Worldwide net sales and revenues decreased 2%, to $12.115 billion, for the fourth quarter of 2026 and increased 4%, to $47.704 billion, for the full year.
Net sales were $10.514 billion for the quarter and $41.292 billion for the year, compared with $10.579 billion and $38.917 billion in fiscal 2025, respectively.

quotes.text: As we enter fiscal 2027, we’re seeing early signs of improvement in large agriculture, led by North America.

items.heading: Our financial results largely depend upon the agricultural market business cycle, as well as general economic conditions and outlook. Negative conditions in the agricultural industry and general economy cause weakened demand for our equipment and services, limit access to funding, and result in higher funding costs.
We face risks associated with international, national, and regional trade laws, regulations, and policies that could materially impair our profitability.
Our international operations expose us to risks and events beyond our control in countries in which we operate.

Changing worldwide demand for food and different forms of renewable energy can impact the price of farm commodities and consequently the demand for our equipment. This could result in higher research and development costs related to changing machine fuel requirements.
Restructuring, rationalization, and relocation of manufacturing facilities may cause capacity constraints, inventory fluctuations, and other issues.
Inability to accurately forecast customer demand for products and services, and to adequately manage inventory, could adversely affect our operating results.
